title: Single-cell imaging and machine learning reveal a Cdk2–COP9 interaction that induces a senescence-like immune state in Drosophila cells
summary: A synthetic genetic-interaction and cell-morphology map covering more than 6,800 Drosophila genes supported machine-learning-based gene-function assignments across 47 modules. In follow-up, Cytoclass single-cell classification revealed a state-specific interaction between Cdk2 and COP9 signalosome knockdown: co-depletion arrested cell-cycle progression and produced a senescence-like phenotype with increased antimicrobial-peptide expression in cultured cells and hemocytes, including without bacterial infection.
ai_technology: Single-cell morphology classifier ensemble and machine-learning analysis of genetic-interaction profiles (Cytoclass; support-vector machines and random forest)
organization: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ); Heidelberg University; University of Applied Sciences Bingen

evidence.tested: A synthetic genetic-interaction and cell-morphology map covering more than 6,800 Drosophila genes supported machine-learning-based gene-function assignments across 47 modules.
evidence.unknown: The findings are from cultured Drosophila cells and hemocytes; they do not establish mammalian or human disease mechanisms. The senescence-like phenotype and antimicrobial-peptide induction were measured after experimental RNAi co-depletion. The global module assignments and many network interactions are computational inferences; only selected interactions received targeted follow-up.
evidence.ai_role: The authors generated single-cell morphology and synthetic genetic-interaction profiles, used machine-learning-based function discovery to assign functions to genes in 47 modules, and applied Cytoclass state classification to reveal interactions hidden in bulk-average profiles. The state-specific Cdk2–COP9 interaction was followed up by double-RNAi assays, single-cell transcriptomics, beta-galactosidase and antimicrobial-peptide measurements.
